post_description: The two causes of rising seas and how fast the rise is accelerating, from NASA and NOAA. Sources: National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://sealevel.nasa.gov/sea-level-101/global-sea-level-rise/the-basics/ and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/sealevel.html #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Why is the ocean creeping higher along the world's coasts? Two things drive it: ocean water expands as it warms, and glaciers and ice sheets on land melt into the sea. Melting sea ice does not raise sea level, because it already floats in the ocean. The ocean soaks up most of the extra heat, and that warming explains less of the rise than melting land ice does. That ice comes from glaciers and the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets. The first 10 centimeters took 90 years, from 1902 to 1992, but the next 10 took just 30 years, from 1993 to 2023.
